news.title: Password manager breach exposes millions — check if your passwords were stolen at haveibeenpwned.com
news.excerpt: A major password manager breach this month exposed millions of stored credentials. Go to haveibeenpwned.com and enter your email to see if your passwords were compromised. If they were, change them immediately on every site where you reused them.

news.title: CISA Adds Two Actively Exploited Zero-Days — Patch These Now
news.excerpt: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday fixed over 1,400 vulnerabilities including two actively exploited zero-days (CVE-2026-96951 in Windows and an Ivanti VPN flaw). Open Settings → Windows Update and install the current cumulative update today.

news.title: FBI Impersonation Scams Hit 61,000 Victims — $1.6 Billion Lost
news.excerpt:
The FBI says scammers impersonating government officials have hit nearly 61,000 people since January 2025, stealing over $1.6 billion. They call or email pretending to be the FBI, IRS, Social Security, or local police — saying you owe money, your identity was stolen, or there's a warrant. They demand payment by wire, gift card, or crypto.

What to do: Hang up. Government agencies never call demanding money or threatening arrest. If you're worried, look up the real number yourself and call back.…

posts.title: Clearwave Fiber expands in Lake City — check if your address qualifies at clearwavefiber.com
posts.summary: Clearwave Fiber is bringing fiber internet to more Lake City neighborhoods. Visit clearwavefiber.com to check if your address qualifies for service.
posts.truth: Fiber is a game-changer for rural areas. If you're stuck on DSL or satellite, this is worth checking.

posts.title: Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education lose security updates after November — check your edition
posts.summary: Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions get their final security update in November 2026. Open Settings > System > About > Windows specifications to see your edition. If you're on 23H2 Enterprise or Education, start planning your upgrade to 24H2 or later.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their Windows edition has an expiration date. I see businesses running 23H2 who think they're fine because "it still works" — but without security patches, one unpatched flaw is all it takes.

posts.title: Daily Brief: CISA adds four exploited flaws + Firefox 159 puts passwords in sidebar automatically
posts.summary: CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities — update Check Point, Arista VeloCloud, and F5 BIG-IP devices now at vendor sites. Firefox 159 Beta now shows saved passwords in the sidebar by default — free update at firefox.com.

posts.title: Run ChatGPT-style AI on your PC free and offline — Jan.ai downloads models in one click
posts.summary: Download Jan.ai free at jan.ai (Windows, Mac, or Linux). Install it, open the Model Hub (the cube icon on the left), and click "Download" on any model — Llama 3.2 3B for older computers (needs about 4 GB memory), Qwen 2.5 7B for newer ones (about 8 GB memory). It runs 100% offline — your conversations never leave your computer. No account, no subscription, no internet required after the model downloads.
posts.truth: People think AI requires a $2,000 graphics card and a PhD. It doesn't. I run Llama 3.2 on a 5-year-old office desktop with 16 GB memory and it's perfectly usable for writing emails, summarizing PDFs, and answering questions. The model lives on your hard drive, not in the cloud.

posts.title: Your free Columbia County library card unlocks the Libby app for free e-books and audiobooks
posts.summary: Visit any Columbia County library branch (Main Library at 308 NW Columbia Ave in Lake City, Fort White Branch, or West Branch) with a photo ID and proof of address. Get a free library card, then access the Libby app for free e-books and audiobooks on your phone or tablet, Career Online High School for a free accredited high school diploma, and the Florida Electronic Library databases for research. All free with your card.
posts.truth: Most people think the library is just for books. It's not — it's a tech support center you've already paid for with your taxes. I've sent customers there for help setting up email, learning video calls, and printing documents when their home printer dies.

posts.title: Stop Windows tracking you free with O&O ShutUp10++ at ooshutup10.com
posts.summary: O&O ShutUp10++ is a free portable tool that lets you disable Windows telemetry, data collection, and tracking in one click. Download from ooshutup10.com.
posts.truth: I run this on every Windows machine that comes through the shop. Takes 30 seconds and stops a massive amount of background data collection.

posts.title: File Explorer now previews HTML files and remembers your folders free in October Windows Update
posts.summary: The October 2026 Windows 11 update (KB5127648) adds HTML file previews in File Explorer and remembers your folder settings. Free via Windows Update.
posts.truth: This is one of those quiet quality-of-life updates that makes a real difference if you work with web files. No more opening files just to see what's in them.

posts.title: CISA adds four actively exploited flaws to must-patch list — Check Point, Arista, and F5 devices at risk
posts.summary: Update Check Point security gateways, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator, and F5 BIG-IP APM devices now — patches at check point.com, arista.com, and f5.com respectively. These four vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-85102, CVE-2026-93616, CVE-2026-93952, CVE-2026-94127) are being actively exploited per CISA's September 22 alert.
posts.truth: Most people think "I don't have enterprise gear, this doesn't apply to me." But if your router runs on any of these platforms — or your IT provider uses them — you're exposed. I've seen small businesses get hit because their managed service provider hadn't patched a VPN gateway in months.

posts.title: Stop fighting weird video formats — VLC Media Player is the free Swiss Army knife that plays literally everything
posts.summary: Download VLC free at videolan.org/vlc — choose "Windows 64-bit" for most computers. Install it, and it will play any video or audio file you throw at it: MKV, AVI, MP4, MOV, FLAC, MP3, DVDs, Blu-rays, network streams, even broken or incomplete downloads. No codec packs, no ads, no tracking, no subscriptions. Ever.
posts.truth: I've seen people pay for "video converter" software to make a file play in Windows Media Player. VLC plays the original file without converting. The only format it struggles with is DRM-protected commercial movies (iTunes, some streaming downloads) — and that's by design, not a bug.

posts.title: Windows can clean up your disk automatically — Storage Sense frees space while you sleep
posts.summary: Turn on Storage Sense at Settings > System > Storage. Flip the switch to On, then click "Storage Sense" to choose how often it runs (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or "When low on disk space") and what to clean: temporary files, Recycle Bin (after 30 days by default), and Downloads folder (if you want). It's free, built into Windows 10 and 11, and runs automatically in the background.
posts.truth: People buy "PC cleaner" software that does exactly what Storage Sense does for free — and the paid ones often delete things they shouldn't. Microsoft's built-in tool is conservative: it only removes files Windows knows are safe to delete.
